body.heading: Questions are doors
paragraphs: Every question opens some doors and closes others. 'How was school?' opens the door to 'Fine.' 'What was the weirdest thing that happened today?' opens the door to a story.
The difference is specificity and surprise. A question someone has to think about for two seconds is a compliment: it says you actually want to know.

body.heading: A few upgrades
paragraphs: Swap 'How are you?' for 'What's been on your mind this week?' Swap 'Did you have fun?' for 'What was the best part?' Swap 'Any news?' for 'What's something you changed your mind about lately?'
Then do the second half of the job: listen to the answer like it matters, and ask the follow-up. The follow-up question is where conversations turn into connections.

description: 'How are you?' gets 'Fine.' Better questions get real answers — and real conversations.
